claim: The Surgical History states that in 129 of 164 recorded evulsions of a lower limb by large projectiles ablations were performed, many of them doubtless the paring and regularization of the soft tissues with removal of splinters rather than legitimate amputations; 76 were operations in the continuity of the leg (56 recoveries, 14 deaths, 6 unknown) and 40 were amputations in the thigh (26 successful, 13 fatal, 1 doubtful).

source.edition: Part III, Volume II, Surgical History, first issue, Washington: Government Printing Office, 1883 (chapters X to XV: lower extremities, miscellaneous injuries, complications, anaesthetics, the medical staff and materia chirurgica, transportation of the wounded)

quote: In 129 of the 164 cases it is noticed that ablations, many of them doubtless resembling merely the paring and regularization of the soft tissues with removal of splinters or sharp projections of bone, rather than legitimate amputations, were performed. ‘Two of these, however, were successful formal disarticulations at the ankle joint, 2 successful amputations at the knee joint, 1 a fatai exarticulation at the hip. Seventy-six, with 56 recoveries, 14 deaths, and 6 unknown terminations, were operations in the continuity of the leg; forty cases, 26 successful, 13 fatal, 1 doubtful, were amputations in the thigh.

data.population: recorded evulsions of one or other lower limb by solid shot, fragments of shell, torpedoes or other large projectiles (164 cases)
data.measure: operations performed (ablations in 129 cases), by level and result

amputations in the thigh: cases, successful, fatal, doubtful

notes: The History states earlier on the same page that of the 164 instances 93 recovered, 62 or 40 per cent. were fatal and in 9 the result was not ascertained (row 183 of wounds-weapons); 62 of 164 is 37.8 per cent., the History prints 40.

claim: The Surgical History states that the gravity of flesh wounds in the lower extremities greatly exceeds that of analogous injuries in the upper limbs, the dangers arising from lesions of the great blood-vessels and nerves, from peri-articular wounds and especially from deep seton wounds and lacerations of the massive muscles of the thigh, and that many perforations of the thigh lightly regarded at the outset present ultimately formidable complications.

source.edition: Part III, Volume II, Surgical History, first issue, Washington: Government Printing Office, 1883 (chapters X to XV: lower extremities, miscellaneous injuries, complications, anaesthetics, the medical staff and materia chirurgica, transportation of the wounded)

quote: The gravity of flesh wounds in the lower extremities greatly exceeds, however, that of analogous injuries in the upper limbs. The dangers arising from lesions of the great blood-vessels and nerves of the lower extremities, from peri-articular wounds, and especially from deep seton wounds and lacerations of the massive muscles of the thigh, are great. Many perforations of the thigh that are lightly regarded at the outset, present ultimately formidable complications.

claim: The Surgical History states that with the clerical force available only a superficial examination of the nearly sixty thousand flesh wounds of the lower extremities was possible: duplicates and cases that proved complicated by contusion of bone or by fracture were sifted out, instances were selected, the average distribution of the wounds in the regions of the limb was determined, and the mortality was ascertained approximately.

source.edition: Part III, Volume II, Surgical History, first issue, Washington: Government Printing Office, 1883 (chapters X to XV: lower extremities, miscellaneous injuries, complications, anaesthetics, the medical staff and materia chirurgica, transportation of the wounded)

quote: It was impossible, with the clerical force available, to make more than a superficial examination of the individual cases of the immense series of nearly sixty-thousand flesh wounds of the lower extremities.” All that has been attempted has been to sift out duplicated cases and those that ultimately proved to be complicated by contusion of bone or by fracture, and to scrutinize the series sufficiently to select instances illustrating the different varieties of injuries of this group, to determine the average distribution of the wounds in the several regions of the limb, and to ascertain approximatively the mortality.

claim: The Surgical History states that of the 58,702 shot wounds of the soft parts of the lower limbs about twenty-six thousand were in the thigh, about twenty-one thousand in the leg and about ten thousand in the foot, as nearly as can be approximated from the hasty field notes and brief hospital entries.

source.edition: Part III, Volume II, Surgical History, first issue, Washington: Government Printing Office, 1883 (chapters X to XV: lower extremities, miscellaneous injuries, complications, anaesthetics, the medical staff and materia chirurgica, transportation of the wounded)

quote: SHOT FLESH WOUNDS.—In the vast series of fifty-eight thousand seven hundred and two cases of shot wounds of the soft parts of the lower limbs placed on the registers, it is difficult in many cases to determine, from the hasty field notes or brief hospital entries, the exact positions and extent of the wounds. As nearly as can be approximated, however, it would appear that about twenty-six thousand of these wounds were in the thigh, about twenty-one thousand in the leg, and about ten thousand in the foot

data.measure: approximate count by seat in the limb
